bibl.note: The supplementary 9 October 2026 adjudication also inspected the University of Illinois copy of the same 1856 printing, Google Books Sm9BAQAAMAAJ, title PP7 and printed pp. 92 and 101. It confirms both adopted readings; the 1741 and 1784 controls are not substituted for 1856.

Book III headings 8 and 15 were directly print-verified on 9 October 2026 against the original 1856 scan and a separately held copy; earlier editions remain distinct controls. The human editor approved the 1856 governing edition and these readings on 9 October 2026.
1856 summary has no terminal point; independently confirmed in Toronto and Illinois copies. Earlier 1741 and 1784 points are edition variants.
Complete 1856 wording and punctuation confirmed in original colour scan and separately held Illinois copy; remove the previous faded-reading hold without importing earlier punctuation.

encodingDesc.p: Printed small capitals transcribed in uppercase; ordinary line-wrap hyphenation joined explicitly; lexical hyphens, spelling, punctuation, brackets and printed footnote pointers retained. Raw digital HTML/XML, scan crops and source bytes remain recoverable. Comparisons may fold case and ae/æ; original source readings are retained without such folding.

normalization.p: Sentence-case presentation is an editorial layer, not a replacement transcription. Each choice retains the exact accepted 1856 text in orig and a case-only display in reg. Proper names, ligatures, punctuation, spelling, source pointers and Roman labels are preserved; common nouns are lowercased. Compiled-index CSS selects reg only, without altering other witnesses.

revisionDesc.change: Supplementary direct print adjudication of III.8 and III.15. Original audit unchanged. All fifteen proposed heading strings preserved; faded-reading qualifications superseded by source-image verification.

Authorized human browser-review correction: one provenance note immediately below the index title; reversible sentence-case readings and left-aligned presentation. Original 1856 readings and existing structural identities remain intact.

div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: Compiled from the chapter headings printed in the Auburn and Rochester edition of Whiston's translation (Alden & Beardsley, 1856). The arrangement as an index is editorial, not an original printed table of contents.

choice.orig: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF TWO YEARS.
choice.reg: Containing the interval of two years.

choice.orig: FROM THE EXODUS OUT OF EGYPT, TO THE REJECTION OF THAT GENERATION.
choice.reg: From the Exodus out of Egypt, to the rejection of that generation.

choice.orig: HOW MOSES, WHEN HE HAD BROUGHT THE PEOPLE OUT OF EGYPT, LED THEM TO MOUNT SINAI; BUT NOT TILL THEY HAD SUFFERED MUCH IN THEIR JOURNEY.
choice.reg: How Moses, when he had brought the people out of Egypt, led them to Mount Sinai; but not till they had suffered much in their journey.

choice.orig: HOW THE AMALEKITES, AND THE NEIGHBOURING NATIONS, MADE WAR WITH THE HEBREWS, AND WERE BEATEN, AND LOST A GREAT PART OF THEIR ARMY.
choice.reg: How the Amalekites, and the neighbouring nations, made war with the Hebrews, and were beaten, and lost a great part of their army.

choice.orig: THAT MOSES KINDLY RECEIVED HIS FATHER-IN-LAW, JETHRO, WHEN HE CAME TO HIM TO MOUNT SINAI.
choice.reg: That Moses kindly received his father-in-law, Jethro, when he came to him to Mount Sinai.

choice.orig: HOW RAGUEL SUGGESTED TO MOSES TO SET HIS PEOPLE IN ORDER, UNDER THEIR RULERS OF THOUSANDS, AND RULERS OF HUNDREDS, WHO LIVED WITHOUT ORDER BEFORE; AND HOW MOSES COMPLIED IN ALL THINGS WITH HIS FATHER-IN-LAW'S ADMONITION.
choice.reg: How Raguel suggested to Moses to set his people in order, under their rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, who lived without order before; and how Moses complied in all things with his father-in-law's admonition.

choice.orig: HOW MOSES ASCENDED UP TO MOUNT SINAI, AND RECEIVED LAWS FROM GOD, AND DELIVERED THEM TO THE HEBREWS.
choice.reg: How Moses ascended up to Mount Sinai, and received laws from God, and delivered them to the Hebrews.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE TABERNACLE WHICH MOSES BUILT IN THE WILDERNESS FOR THE HONOUR OF GOD, AND WHICH SEEMED TO BE A TEMPLE.
choice.reg: Concerning the tabernacle which Moses built in the wilderness for the honour of God, and which seemed to be a temple.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE GARMENTS OF THE PRIESTS, AND OF THE HIGH-PRIEST.
choice.reg: Concerning the garments of the priests, and of the high-priest.

choice.orig: THE MANNER OF OUR OFFERING SACRIFICES.
choice.reg: The manner of our offering sacrifices.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE FESTIVALS; AND HOW EACH DAY OF SUCH FESTIVAL IS TO BE OBSERVED.
choice.reg: Concerning the festivals; and how each day of such festival is to be observed.

choice.orig: HOW MOSES REMOVED FROM MOUNT SINAI, AND CONDUCTED THE PEOPLE TO THE BORDERS OF THE CANAANITES.
choice.reg: How Moses removed from Mount Sinai, and conducted the people to the borders of the Canaanites.

choice.orig: HOW MOSES SENT SOME PERSONS TO SEARCH OUT THE LAND OF THE CANAANITES, AND THE LARGENESS OF THEIR CITIES; AND FARTHER, THAT WHEN THOSE WHO WERE SENT WERE RETURNED, AFTER FORTY DAYS, AND REPORTED THAT THEY SHOULD NOT BE A MATCH FOR THEM, AND EXTOLLED THE STRENGTH OF THE CANAANITES, THE MULTITUDE WERE DISTURBED, AND FELL INTO DESPAIR; AND WERE RESOLVED TO STONE MOSES, AND TO RETURN BACK AGAIN INTO EGYPT, AND SERVE THE EGYPTIANS.
choice.reg: How Moses sent some persons to search out the land of the Canaanites, and the largeness of their cities; and farther, that when those who were sent were returned, after forty days, and reported that they should not be a match for them, and extolled the strength of the Canaanites, the multitude were disturbed, and fell into despair; and were resolved to stone Moses, and to return back again into Egypt, and serve the Egyptians.

choice.orig: HOW MOSES WAS DISPLEASED AT THIS, AND FORETOLD THAT GOD WAS ANGRY, AND THAT THEY SHOULD CONTINUE IN THE WILDERNESS FOR FORTY YEARS, AND NOT, DURING THAT TIME, EITHER RETURN INTO EGYPT, OR TAKE POSSESSION OF CANAAN.
choice.reg: How Moses was displeased at this, and foretold that God was angry, and that they should continue in the wilderness for forty years, and not, during that time, either return into Egypt, or take possession of Canaan.
